# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 12

**1** "Those from the third mountain, which was full of thorns and briars — who are they?" "These are those who believe, but some of them are rich, and some are engaged in many business dealings; the briars are the rich, and the thorns are those who are engaged in various business transactions. These therefore do not adhere to the servants of God, but they are choked by their own transactions and riches, and they are separated from the righteous. **2** Some therefore of them give to the poor; others share nothing of what they possess. Those who share are given salvation, but those who do not share are rejected. **3** Those from the fourth mountain, which had thorns at the top but the lower portions were green — these are the double-minded who are not entirely righteous, as well as those who have faith but who have great wealth. These are for the greater part unrighteous, yet some repentance is given to them because their green parts were not entirely dead. **4** Those from the fifth mountain, which had green grass and was rugged — these are those who believe and are righteous, but they are hard-hearted and self-willed and desire to know all things, yet they know nothing. **5** Because of their self-will and empty cleverness they quarrel among themselves; and they think they know everything, but they are the most ignorant of all. Because of this foolish pride they became evil and fell away from the truth. **6** Yet there is repentance for them; for they are not wicked but rather foolish and without sense. If they repent they will live to God; but if they do not repent, they will dwell with the women who do evil to them."

---

*EMET note: Mountains 3-5. Mountain 3 = the entangled wealthy; Mountain 4 = the double-minded; Mountain 5 = the arrogantly self-willed. The thorn/briar imagery echoes Mark 4:18-19 (the thorns that choke the word).*
